(1) Droplet digital PCR is highly sensitive and specific for LGR detection and is a promising alternative to the MLPA assay.
the droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) method is a reliable tool in the detection of BRCA1 large genomic rearrangments (LGRs).

the droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a reliable tool that enables the detection of large BRCA1 genomic rearrangements and can be used as a screening method in the high-risk breast/ovarian cancer families.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of ddPCR assay for the detection of LGR in BRCA1 gene, which is based on the use the commercially available primers and probes and requires no additional reagents or equipment.
the development of the novel assay and the identification of novel recurrent LGRs in Russian BC/OC families.
the detection of BRCA1 LGRs in Russian patients with hereditary BC, which is the first report of this kind.

LGRs of BRCA1 are rare, with an estimated frequency of 1.3–1.5% in the studied population.
the exon 8 deletion is a rare event in the general population and should not be considered as a founder mutation in the Russian population.
the prevalence of BRCA1 LGRs in Russian population is about 0.5%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency of exon 8 loss in BRCA1 gene was 0.7% in BC and OC patients.
exon 8 deletion in BRCA1 gene is a rare event in the Russian population.
the deletion of exon 8 of BRCA1 is a rare but recurrent event in BC/OC patients, and the deletion is not necessarily associated with other large genomic rearrangemets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exon 8 deletion of BRCA1, which was previously considered as a single event, is in fact a part of two distinct large genomic rearrangments.
the exon 8 copy number assay may be used as a first-line test to screen for BRCA1 LGRs.
the exon 8 loss is a recurrent BRCA1 mutation, which can be detected by MLPA or ddPCR.
